text:
maria: Heads up — the model A/B matrix shows v3.2 (kernel-heuristic changes) with a ~12% p95 token latency regression vs v3.1 on route /chat/compose. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/ab?panel=token_waterfall Can we triage?
kevin: Thanks — timeline? did the v3.2 rollout overlap with any batching heuristic flips or KV cache config changes?
infra-bot: deploy: v3.2 canary started 1945678800 by deploy-bot, set rollout=20% (region=us-west).
jamal: quick profile dump from the canary window (extract):
```
[PROF] 2026-03-18T12:05:12Z kernel_select: v2_matmul chosen 37% of calls, fallback v1_matmul 63%
[PROF] seq_len_bucket>1024: fallback_rate=89%
[PROF] avg_kernel_time_ms: v2_matmul=0.9, v1_matmul=1.6
```
jamal: looks like kernel chooser is taking the slower path for high-seq tokens more often now.
olivia: Also seeing KV cache hit drop during same window: kv_prefix_hit 92% -> 68% (10:00-12:10). That amplifies token cost because more KV fetches + fallback kernel compounding.
kevin: interesting — so two interacting regressions: kernel selection shift + lower prefix cache. Any config flips for batching windows or prefix eviction?
maria: I toggled batching_mode -> adaptive_dynamic on canary earlier today (intent was to reduce tail latency). Maybe that changed batch shape distribution.
jamal: adaptive_dynamic increases batch length variance which can push sequences into >1024 bucket mid-batch; kernel selector heuristic was tuned for more uniform shapes, so it chooses safe fallback more.
kevin: can you run a focused micro-benchmark? Command: `./tools/perf_bench --model v3.2 --route /chat/compose --qps 60 --seq 512 --duration 300 --trace kernel_select,kv_hit`
maria: Ran it — pasted summary: p50=18ms, p95=72ms, kv_hit=71%, kernel_fallback_pct=58% (run at 60 qps).
kevin: compare against v3.1 run (same command) result: p50=17ms, p95=64ms, kv_hit=91%, kernel_fallback_pct=22%. So delta matches observed 12% p95 regression.
olivia: short-term mitigations: 1) drop canary to 5% 2) pin /chat/compose traffic to v3.1 via routing rule 3) temporarily revert adaptive_dynamic batching. Which do we want?
kevin: I vote revert batching toggle first (lowest blast radius) and flip kernel selector config to prefer v1_matmul for seq>512 until selector is retuned.
jamal: I'll open a PR with selector tuning and simulation data. Need a few hours for a safe knob.
maria: Olivia can you do the rollback of batching flag? If yes we'll monitor dashboard for kv_hit and token waterfall.
olivia: On it — rolling batching_mode -> adaptive_static for v3.2 canary now. Roll started 1945680000. Will watch metrics.
perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/1945678901 — major hot path: kv_fetch + v1_matmul in sequence >1024.
kevin: great. After we stabilize, follow-ups: 1) add dashboard split: token waterfall broken down by kernel implementation (v1/v2) 2) per-route KPI alert when kv_hit drops >10% 3) gate kernel selector changes behind offline sim matching traffic distribution.
maria: Agreed. I'm also going to add a small synthetic test to CI that runs the `--seq 256/512/1536` shapes to catch regressions early.
olivia: metrics are reflecting improvement ~10 mins after toggle: kv_hit up to 88%, p95 down to ~66ms. I'll keep canary at 10% for 30m then reassess.
kevin: thanks everyone. jamal please ping here when selector PR is ready. :thumbsup:
